answer: Each seat is a crane whose ferrous wire rope is the credential. It carries a stamped ferrule and a sealed hour meter. Every 200 hours a rigger calipers six points on the strands, which spiral around the core. Each epoch the seed names a zone; the seat photographs the ferrule beside the caliper, and the ledger checks it against that rope's wear curve. Two seats on one ferrule or chassis plate collapse to one vote and forfeit 45,000 POA each. A rope runs $2,400, a survey $180, so 1,000 clones need 1,000 ropes. Wear hits its nadir at one zone; a groove never cut cannot be photographed.
